title: Nut-Free Chocolate Fudge Swirl Cupcakes
shortDescription: Moist cocoa cupcakes with a silky fudge frosting swirl, ready in about 43 minutes and safe for nut-free school treats.
description: These cupcakes came out of a real problem: my son's class needed a nut-free treat that still tasted rich. I tested this cocoa base three times to get a soft, moist crumb without any nut flours or oils. The frosting is where the fudge flavor lives. It uses melted chocolate and cocoa powder together, so it swirls high but stays soft enough to eat with a fork, not a knife. I keep this recipe on hand for bake sales and birthday parties. Every ingredient is easy to check against a nut-free label, which makes party planning simpler. You do not need special equipment. A hand mixer, one bowl for wet ingredients, and a piping bag get the job done.
ingredients: 4 oz semisweet chocolate, melted and cooled
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a 12-cup muffin pan with paper liners.
Whisk flour, cocoa powder, baking soda, and salt in a bowl. Set aside.
Beat softened butter with both sugars until light and fluffy, about 2 minutes.
Add eggs one at a time, then mix in vanilla extract.
Alternate adding the flour mix and buttermilk, mixing just until combined.
Stir in hot water last. The batter will look thin, and that is correct.
Divide batter among liners, filling each about two-thirds full.
Bake 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool in the pan 5 minutes, then move to a wire rack.
For frosting, beat butter until smooth, then add melted chocolate and mix well.
Add powdered sugar in two batches, alternating with heavy cream, until frosting is smooth and pipeable.
Pipe a tall swirl onto each fully cooled cupcake using a large open star tip.
tips: Cool cupcakes completely before frosting or the swirl will slide off.
Check your chocolate chips or bars for a nut-free certification if this is for a school event.
If frosting feels too soft to pipe, chill it for 10 minutes before swirling.
Use room temperature eggs and buttermilk so the batter mixes evenly.

faq.question: Are these cupcakes safe for a nut-free classroom?
faq.answer: Yes, as long as you check your cocoa powder, chocolate, and butter brands for nut-free labeling. None of the ingredients in this recipe contain nuts by default.

faq.question: Why does the batter look so thin before baking?
faq.answer: The hot water thins the batter on purpose. It keeps the cake moist and helps the cocoa flavor bloom, and it bakes up fully firm.

faq.question: Can I make the frosting ahead of time?
faq.answer: Yes, store it in the fridge for up to 3 days in a sealed container. Bring it to room temperature and re-whip for a few seconds before piping.

faq.question: Can I turn this into a layer cake instead?
faq.answer: Yes, this batter works in two 8 inch round pans. Bake for 28 to 32 minutes and cool fully before frosting.

conclusion: This recipe earns a spot in my regular rotation because it is simple and school safe. The fudge swirl on top makes plain cocoa cupcakes feel like a real treat.
